reads.worst: It relies on a polling queue and gateway/session behavior, and retries can complicate operational diagnosis when a chat is unavailable.

reads.best: A counterfactual record/rewind/edit/replay debugger built on Hermes's llm/tool middleware: something new for agents, that only a plugin can do.
reads.worst: The author's own notes say a real child replay is untested end-to-end; an edit before the branch point does nothing, and traces store unredacted prompts and tool results on disk.

reads.best: Default-deny identity checks and transactional grants, verification and revocation are backed by adversarial and concurrency tests.
reads.worst: Access control is cooperative within one installation: shell-capable agents can bypass the path trip-wire, and revocation cannot retract facts already copied into conversation or external memory.

reads.best: A substantial platform and polished social UI enforce model budgets in code and separate tool-free room agents from the owner’s full Hermes agent.
reads.worst: Nostr signing secrets are generated and read from the plugin’s own unencrypted SQLite identity record instead of Hermes’s secret store, and shared toys retain disclosed network-isolation gaps.

reads.best: Uses hooks that rewrite messages, tool arguments and results, which a skill cannot do, and its README honestly lists coverage gaps.
reads.worst: Does not cover CLI/TUI/Desktop input, uses its own vault rather than Hermes's secret store, and on non-Windows falls back to a dev-only key file.

reads.best: User-initiated, consent-first desktop context capture on Windows, macOS and Linux with a fail-closed password-manager exclude list, secret redaction, a companion token via the secret route, and 61 tests.
reads.worst: Depends on the cua-driver binary and OS accessibility grants, with an 1,800-line core module and a separate companion process that make setup and review harder.

reads.best: The integrated failure-to-diagnosis-to-fix workflow includes source excerpts, stale-result detection, passing-command resolution, Desktop controls and meaningful Python and JavaScript tests.
reads.worst: The pinned file tools omit Hermes's sensitive-file denylist, allowing credential files within the chosen cwd, and search opens file symlinks without checking their resolved containment ([backstop_core.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/themahis/hermes-backstop/99fd96995d363de92050fdf61a902979b5926f1e/backstop_core.py)).

reads.best: Deterministic receipt capture and output hooks tackle misleading completion claims without another model or network service.
reads.worst: Claim matching uses broad regexes and the latest category receipt, so a successful narrow or merely test-labelled command can incorrectly verify an all-tests claim.

reads.best: Novel use of api_request hooks to make Hermes run on user's own sleeping hardware, bounded and fail-safe.
reads.worst: Single ~1000-line file, README thin relative to complex config forms.

reads.best: The code separates model draft/read operations from a foreground human confirmation flow, records durable receipts, and clearly explains its limits as recordkeeping rather than an execution gate.
reads.worst: It is a specialist governance ledger with a manual Linux foreground-console workflow; its own documentation says same-user database access can bypass application checks.

reads.best: Integrates native Messages, Responses and Chat Completions routing with Hermes caching, reasoning settings and billing-aware fallback behavior.
reads.worst: The process-global model catalog is not keyed by base URL, so profiles using different gateways can reuse the wrong endpoint's model metadata.

reads.best: Exact workspace trust, single-use request-bound approvals, bounded subprocesses and receipt verification form a substantial engineering integration.
reads.worst: Setup needs a separate Kujo runtime and numerous pinned source checkouts, with browser, container and producer-binding gaps explicitly remaining.

reads.best: Shared task records, git history, constitution projections, and room wakeups connect persistent user context across sessions, subagents, and Desktop.
reads.worst: The pinned release reads Hermes .env directly, forwards the gateway environment to external Agora code, and lets newly edited scheduled jobs run without renewed operator approval.

reads.best: Owner identity checks, canonical destinations and crash-resistant approval claims give real enforcement rather than a model’s promise to ask first.
reads.worst: Preventing alternate write paths requires a dedicated restrictive profile and a separate launcher tied to Hermes 0.23.1 internals, with manual connector declarations.

reads.best: Automatic capture, user-only closure, persistent reminders and shared-chat privacy handling solve a real agent memory gap.
reads.worst: The append-only plaintext ledger grows indefinitely and shared-chat ownership has a documented timing ambiguity.

reads.best: It fills a real gap (finding the file in ~/Downloads) entirely offline, with a secret denylist, symlink and decompression-bomb guards, 30 stdlib tests and an honest-limits section.
reads.worst: recall_forget only deletes index rows, so the session-start refresh brings a forgotten folder back, and recall_open reads any non-denylisted absolute path up to 64 MB, even outside the indexed roots.

reads.best: The migration preserves existing tool names while testing secret scope, backpressure, and platform registration.
reads.worst: It serves one messaging platform and is a migration of existing Hermes functionality rather than a new agent capability.

reads.best: A substantial Desktop workflow combines original-record evidence, explicit private-model opt-in, human-confirmed transfer suggestions and security regression tests without moving funds.
reads.worst: Protected reviews need an external vault secret and in-process loading, while live exchange matching and complete history coverage are explicitly limited.

reads.best: Integrates with the memory-provider lifecycle and returns original records with session IDs and excerpt offsets rather than only lossy summaries.
reads.worst: Setup guidance is thin, Windows cannot load its fcntl store, and absolute zero-hallucination claims exceed a lexical matcher plus optional generated answers.

reads.best: It extends the actual composer through SDK surfaces, with immediate local suggestions and careful stale-response handling.
reads.worst: No test suite ships, editor detection reaches into core DOM, and the model fallback rejects Arabic output despite the advertised RTL support.

reads.best: Public subagent lifecycle calls and usage hooks make model delegation, cancellation and per-run cost accounting more capable than a workflow prompt.
reads.worst: Escalation is passed the full original budget rather than the remainder, and rejected tool narrowing automatically retries with all parent tools.

reads.best: The rich Desktop integration is backed by bounded, rate-limited feed clients, Hermes secret storage and extensive tests for member-data isolation.
reads.worst: Its core signal engine is a hosted dependency outside the pinned code, and many guarded private Hermes imports create maintenance risk.

reads.best: 44 test functions across unit/integration/acceptance suites, a pre_tool_call guard that blocks raw ssh calls to registered hosts, and a documented private-API disclosure (docs/PUBLIC-SURFACE.md).
reads.worst: Dangerous commands route through Hermes's own approval classifier rather than the plugin forcing approval on every remote command, so safety depends on that classifier being well tuned.

reads.best: Its approval binds an exact destination and inventory fingerprint, while uncertain uploads are reconciled before another write.
reads.worst: The provider profiles and real Gmail migration were not live-tested at the pinned commit, and setup demands Google OAuth plus operator configuration.

reads.best: Hooks enforce a spend budget and the README is honest about estimates and limits; has tests.
reads.worst: Cannot stop the reply already generating, no Desktop UI or screenshots.

reads.best: Deterministic time-zone and DST handling that models get wrong, with a bundled tzdb, core and integration tests, and a heavily polished Desktop page with real screenshots.
reads.worst: Meeting-time conversion is a well-trodden idea, and much of the release effort goes to animation, artwork and music rather than to the tools.

reads.best: Thorough: 134 tests, standard library only, paths kept inside the project, and SSRF-safe url_loads with pinned addresses checked on every redirect hop.
reads.worst: The README says only the user can add url_loads checks, but the model can write lastgood-config.json directly; the repo is cluttered with build logs and AI-review notes, and there is no UI.

reads.best: It is unusually thorough about detecting leaks across hooks, transcripts, SQLite stores, histories, and explicit limitations.
reads.worst: A detected or blocked string automatically triggers destructive rewrites of chat and shell history by default, so a false positive can alter data without a separate approval.

reads.best: Small and clean: key read only through Hermes's secret scope, clear errors, mocked-network tests and a plain what-it-does-on-your-machine section.
reads.worst: One paid third-party API, with no screenshots and little novelty.

reads.best: Implements a complete preview-and-install product with checksum and archive-path validation, paused packed routines, screenshots, and extensive safety tests.
reads.worst: The installer copies self-indexed bundles without re-sanitizing config or pausing imported cron jobs, so a hand-built bundle can activate unsafe behavior despite its preview; it also directly reads .env files.

reads.best: A substantial Desktop studio, version-bound drafts, take provenance, audio checks and broad regression tests make it feel like a product for local music creation.
reads.worst: The reachable cloud-setup routes save and read API keys in cloud-keys.json instead of Hermes secrets, a catalog-policy problem despite the otherwise substantial implementation; see [credential code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KeyArgo/hermes-music-studio/e0fa23a5f16092a040feb575bd878aab8f687c28/music_studio/setup.py).

reads.best: Uses transactional budget reservations and Hermes approval directives, with scoped test-mode Stripe secrets and concurrency tests.
reads.worst: The pinned tree commits prohibited Python bytecode, and third-party retries awaiting approval can each proceed because only its own payment handler atomically claims a reservation.

reads.best: Novel inter-session agent messaging with very heavy test coverage.
reads.worst: Relies on private host APIs, delivery is not exactly-once, and the shipped Desktop file renders nothing.

reads.best: Dependency-free image comparison includes separate change regions, masks, declared-change contracts and focused browser and decoder tests.
reads.worst: The verification hook only notices stored FAIL or REVIEW verdicts, so a capture error after a prior PASS leaves no failing gate; Chrome sandboxing may also be disabled automatically.

reads.best: Its browser loop persists chats and routes offers and personal details through a human approval gate.
reads.worst: The commitment guard is regex-based, real company chats are untested, and phone-call safety largely depends on the external voice agent following instructions.

reads.best: It reaches the physical world safely: a real preflight with a to-scale Desktop pane marking each issue, and payment only through a link a person opens and pays on Stripe.
reads.worst: The package has no tests, the work depends on the entrant's own API on a workers.dev host that receives the user's PDF and address, the server is one 838 KB bundled file, and it covers only flyers in the contiguous US.

reads.best: A fresh idea, paying down 'comprehension debt' by quizzing the user on agent-written code built from the real diffs, with a lines-understood score.
reads.worst: The pull request says it is 'Not yet verified with a live model', and the questions and grading rest entirely on LLM prompts.

reads.best: Provides Desktop previews, secret scanning, safe archive extraction, paused schedules, disabled MCP servers, and approval hooks.
reads.worst: Despite these safeguards, upload and unshare read management credentials from shared.json rather than Hermes secret storage, conflicting with catalog rule 11.

reads.best: Concrete replay, fuzzing and crawl primitives produce measured evidence rather than asking the model to invent security findings.
reads.worst: Session credentials are stored in plaintext identities.json outside Hermes secret storage, and DNS authorization is separated from the later connection lookup.

reads.best: Privacy-conscious audit records and fresh per-event approval keys are backed by adversarial tests and clear audit-versus-enforcement semantics.
reads.worst: Its classifier recognizes only a tiny terminal grammar; enforcement blocks routine unknown tools, audit mode does not enforce, and neither mode proves actual execution or provides a sandbox.

reads.best: Uses real pre-tool block/approval directives and a tested integer-cent policy engine rather than asking the model to obey a budget.
reads.worst: Detection is heuristic and the ledger has no atomic reservation for concurrent spends, so parallel calls can exceed the daily cap and dynamically constructed payments can evade detection.

reads.best: Its discovery loop and broad normalized crypto-tool catalog can save an agent from stitching together many providers.
reads.worst: The submitted package is primarily remote configuration and skills, so correctness, availability and much of the security boundary depend on a proprietary hosted service outside the pinned code.

reads.best: The middleware intervenes before results reach the model, with envelope escaping, report mode and tests for benign-content preservation.
reads.worst: Enforce mode rebuilds flagged output from only the first 200,000 characters by default, silently dropping the remaining content; later-only attacks are not scanned.

reads.best: It makes existing markdown plans usable as a session-aware progress interface, with content-hash checks on checkbox edits and extensive parser and Desktop tests.
reads.worst: At the pinned commit, POST and DELETE /block pass unchecked IDs into JSON filenames, allowing path traversal and modification of files outside the plugin data directory.

reads.best: Uses bounded per-session state, cooldowns and extensive regression tests, while keeping failure annotations out of known unattended runs and untrusted results.
reads.worst: Its intervention is mainly skill advice, and annotating attended failures resets result hashes and delays core stall/cycle notices, as the README explicitly discloses.

reads.best: Persistent loop state, stall budgets, branch guards and failure analysis go well beyond a single coding prompt.
reads.worst: The model-callable loop_approve tool directly adds commands to Hermes permanent approval allowlist, and card approvals accept comment text without verifying a human author.

reads.best: Deterministic, honest verdicts from official APIs, an optional GitHub token from the secret store, escaped HTML reports and 19 offline tests.
reads.worst: Keyword matching on three public sources is a shallow demand signal, and there is no UI beyond the /radar command and the report.

reads.best: Careful bridge code: https-only webhook stored as a Hermes secret, redirects refused, path-traversal checks on job ids, and 20 tests including a manifest-matches-registration check.
reads.worst: The specialists are just system prompts a skill could carry, and the Grok Bot half is a generic webhook POST plus a shared folder because Grok Bot has no API, so little of it is specific to Hermes or Grok Bot.

reads.best: Scientifically honest output: pixel counts, confidence intervals, distinct no-data vs service-down statuses, and band downloads locked to one https host.
reads.worst: It downloads whole band files (four per query, up to 600 s each) and fetches terrain point by point, so one call can run many minutes and pull close to 1 GB; the README is short and has no screenshots.

reads.best: The readable runtime has schema-validated tools, permission-aware catalogs and tests, while the portable manifest declares the server untrusted.
reads.worst: Installation requires a separate daemon/runtime and its own configuration credentials; the pinned Hermes package is chiefly MCP metadata and skills.

reads.best: Explicit missing-data abstention, bounded opt-in networking and extensive evidence/chronology tests make its research boundaries unusually clear.
reads.worst: Ticker-only research lacks automatic fundamentals and holdings, relies on an unofficial endpoint, and its heuristic recommendations remain unvalidated.

reads.best: The portable manifest explicitly marks the remote server untrusted, supporting human approval for write tools.
reads.worst: The pinned deliverable contains configuration and skills only, with no server implementation or automated tests to substantiate the advertised remote capabilities.

reads.best: Clear Hermes-specific setup and disclosures include an untrusted-server declaration to gate the email-based full-audit request.
reads.worst: The installed hermes folder is a remote connector rather than the audit engine, so the pinned package cannot establish hosted-check reliability or privacy behavior.

reads.best: The relay code in the repo root compares tokens in constant time, rejects Origin headers, and blocks private-address image fetches, with about 90 tests.
reads.worst: The plugin installs none of that code; the README says it 'was not run against a live Hermes process', the token is also kept on disk, and the browser download is unverified.

reads.best: A real provider backend handles schema mapping, scoped secrets, bounded polling and non-retried paid submissions with offline regression coverage.
reads.worst: Generation spends credits without an approval prompt or computed total, and a failed download is silently returned as a successful remote URL.

reads.best: Fixed read-only PowerShell queries normalize localized dates, singleton collections and signed HRESULTs into useful diagnostic results.
reads.worst: Combining only_failures with a title query that excludes actual failures incorrectly reports that every update in the window ended clean.

reads.best: The package declares a Hermes secret and authenticated MCP header, documents per-call credit costs and gives detailed lookup examples and limitations. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/khmuhtadin/api-indonesia-examples/73d9d4bc060ad4814d0c95c9b3f5f328d07858d5/README.md)
reads.worst: The actual tools, data freshness and error handling are served remotely outside the pinned repository, which contains examples and configuration but no server tests. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/khmuhtadin/api-indonesia-examples/73d9d4bc060ad4814d0c95c9b3f5f328d07858d5/README.md)

reads.best: Readable dependency-free handlers provide live-data lookup, short caching, secret-store integration and a data-only fallback when the model is unavailable.
reads.worst: It is mainly a single-service wrapper; native-asset filtering is heuristic, and tests use fixtures and a fake model rather than Hermes integration.

reads.best: Uses Hermes-managed OAuth and untrusted-server approvals, with explicit recipient-and-text confirmation guidance.
reads.worst: The pinned package contains configuration and a skill only; the actual tools run remotely and cannot be audited at this commit.

reads.best: Uses Hermes provider profiles directly with no dependencies or custom credential persistence.
reads.worst: The pinned manifest omits requires_env for SYNAP_API_KEY, leaving installer key setup undeclared, and its three stub-based tests verify profile constants rather than real Hermes integration.

reads.best: Provenance-backed memory where AI-proposed facts wait in a human review queue, with OAuth handled by Hermes's own MCP client so the package holds no secrets.
reads.worst: The package is two manifests and a 53-line skill with no code or tests; all behaviour lives in a proprietary paid service that the plugin cannot show or verify.

reads.best: A clearly documented portable package offers a pinned connector version, terminal setup and an explicit disclosure of local token storage.
reads.worst: The connector reads and refreshes file-backed OAuth tokens outside Hermes credential routes, leaving the catalog rule 11 admission issue unresolved ([Code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/davidmosiah/fitbit-mcp/c669895c6c96ded8c35978c7461c02dbed7fa0fc/src/services/fitbit-client.ts)).

reads.best: Marks the MCP server untrusted so writes need approval.
reads.worst: No code or tests, and the docs contradict the config (DOOP_MCP_URL is never read; it says Node is needed, but nothing uses it).

reads.best: Honest README with screenshots, per-session state, and clear statement that it is a soft constraint.
reads.worst: Only a prompt prefix; does not enforce read-only, no tests, and no backend code.

reads.best: The public connector needs no key and keeps actual ticket purchase and event publication in a person-completed flow.
reads.worst: Only manifests, connection configuration and a skill are pinned; remote tool implementation and tests are absent, while organizer management in the README needs a separate connection.

reads.best: The connector has a small local attack surface and clearly describes read-only, business-scoped reporting.
reads.worst: The pinned package contains configuration and a skill, with no server implementation or tests to establish remote reliability and no campaign management capability.

reads.best: The workflows clearly separate reporting, commission review, coupon setup, troubleshooting, and payouts, with confirmation language around mutations.
reads.worst: The repository contains no implementation or tests for the hosted service and depends on an npx-downloaded bridge, so the pinned plugin cannot establish end-to-end reliability offline.

reads.best: Bundled canonical markup and census-backed class checks help agents avoid inventing design-system components without a service or API key.
reads.worst: The validator only recognizes double-quoted lowercase class attributes and style blocks, misses equivalent HTML and inline CSS, and ships no tests; the README also incorrectly calls it skills-only.

reads.best: The documentation clearly distinguishes estimated revenue ranges, paid tools and quotas, and openly discloses the remote-only implementation. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mmdincer/apphitlist-mcp/a7ef3444bd7b6821f34908e802a71a2fdde06e50/README.md)
reads.worst: At this pin mcp.json supplies no Authorization header and the setup examples target other clients, leaving a Hermes catalog install unable to authenticate; server code and tests are also absent. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mmdincer/apphitlist-mcp/a7ef3444bd7b6821f34908e802a71a2fdde06e50/mcp.json)

reads.best: The pipeline is a practical combination of narration, timed camera motion and video rendering for demos.
reads.worst: It has no tests, depends on several external executables/services, writes to a fixed home directory and sends model-supplied narration to ElevenLabs.

reads.best: The local deterministic builder, complete lane sweep tests and reproducible demo make a narrow music-production workflow unusually well documented.
reads.worst: check_lyrics collects contradictory dynamic tags but never adds them to issues, so a contradictory draft can still return ok=true.

reads.best: It uses OAuth, labels the remote server untrusted, and documents that writes and sends need approval.
reads.worst: The pinned package contains no implementation or tests; it downloads an npx bridge and delegates its changing tool set to a hosted service outside the commit.

reads.best: Tiny, readable, local-only stdlib code with an honest three-way result (holds, broken, no seal) and a selftest.
reads.worst: The seal is an unkeyed hash stored next to the file, so whoever edits the file can simply re-seal it: it catches accidents, not tampering, which is less than the README's claim to 'prove' a handoff was not changed, and sha256sum in a skill would do the same.

reads.best: Covers the marketplace's full buy/sell loop, and the API key comes from Hermes's secret store first.
reads.worst: It moves money (hire_gig, approve releases escrow) with no approval gate in the plugin, can upload any local file, and /operate demo writes a fake +$68 that /operate status then shows as Net Earned; there are no tests.

reads.best: It exposes a full fax workflow with an untrusted MCP declaration and an approval-oriented skill.
reads.worst: The actual service code is remote; portable use invokes an npm package at runtime, and live stdio loading was not tested.

reads.best: The package declares the remote server untrusted and documents the separate OAuth setup and verification step.
reads.worst: All functional tools run on a changeable remote server; OAuth needs manual native configuration, and local tests mostly check packaging and mocked responses.

reads.best: The public template catalog is reachable through a simple remote MCP declaration without a local service or account setup.
reads.worst: The read-only manifest and skill contradict the README and bundled proxy’s account and generation operations, and the proxy has no request timeout or shipped automated tests.

reads.best: Marks the server untrusted and needs no key.
reads.worst: No code, minimal docs, one of 100 templated near-identical entries.

reads.best: The README clearly explains installation, the audit workflow, data destinations, and consent for inquiries, and the manifest marks the remote server untrusted.
reads.worst: The package contains no audit implementation or tests, and its own skill already calls the same service directly over HTTP without the plugin.

reads.best: Detailed workflows demand clinic-provided figures and site evidence, distinguish uncertainty, and avoid needing patient data.
reads.worst: The package adds only two Markdown skills with no executable integration, so a prompt or skill can provide its entire capability.

reads.best: A credential-free read-only connection makes a focused job dataset available with simple filtering guidance.
reads.worst: The pinned repository contains only configuration and a skill, no server implementation or tests; runtime tools are remote and the PR reports no Hermes installation test.

reads.best: It provides dated primary-filing links and explicitly labels its output as an estimate requiring verification ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Oko300/RiskPulse/fd812147886fcfac5d7e024410a7dfcef255ed16/tools/eight_k.py)).
reads.worst: The 8-K item list is never populated, so the advertised material-event analysis is a filing-count heuristic rather than examination of the disclosed events ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Oko300/RiskPulse/fd812147886fcfac5d7e024410a7dfcef255ed16/tools/eight_k.py)).
